record_notes.DCP-LETT-1556: March 1, 1854 outgoing Darwin letter, not incoming Hooker. First volume finished yesterday evening; second volume not yet certified read. The February 26 Hooker letter 1557 was received this morning. Repeats its past/phantom and meridian language, responds to lifelong ambition and dedication, Tasmania grant, sold-out edition and wife long walk; P8 responds to Lyell lava question. Extended independent book review and Sulivan command news are included in this same answer. Pride in my Book means the dedicated Hooker work, not Darwin authorship. Suggested revision, hypothetical emigration and future Hooker fame are not completed events. Catalogue ID 1556 does not put this before 1557.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1558: March 10, 1854 Darwin has now finished second volume and asks distinct questions about Himalayan Tertiary formations relative to glaciation/elevation, recency of moraines, and beauty of lower Himalayan vegetation compared with Brazil. Emma has begun the book. Stansbury and governess reading of Wallace still incomplete in the current report; later March 23 entry is separate. Printing completion in two or three months is an expectation, not the later July 15 revision finish. Khasia/Blue Mountains comparison is tentative. These questions are answered in surviving 1559; no preserved new incoming prompt for 1558.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1559: Only pages III and IV survive, beginning and ending mid-sentence. Circa March 25 is conjectured from March 26 receipt; XML exact numeric bounds must not erase circa uncertainty. Opening reports Humboldt news, including his not yet receiving Hooker book and anger at Quarterly review; Humboldt did not ask the glacier questions here. P2–5 answer Darwin 1558 on recent moraines, vegetation advancing behind ice, Thomson account of fossiliferous lake silt/glacial detritus and older Siwalik hills. P6 Chilean coloured views shown by Brown and P7 comparison favouring Brazil/Khasia/Chittagong finish fragment. Thomson explanations are attributed, and Darwin later corrected Thomas to Thomson in separate annotation. No full opening, conclusion, Club discussion or Gray enclosure is reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1562: March 26, 1854 expressly acknowledges the long Hooker letter received this morning. The surviving glacier and Humboldt sections of 1559 identify the source, but missing portions would be needed for full Club/reform, anomalous genera, introductory-work and Henslow news prompts. Accept only surviving-response scope. Philosophical Club attendance is conditional on election and health; April election and later resignation are editorial future. P4 proves reading an Asa Gray-to-Hooker letter forwarded by Hooker; footnotes identify February 21 and quote limited passages, not a complete preserved incoming letter. Darwin own species fears, criticism of Agassiz and proposed book return remain his words. Return Wednesday with onward Thursday delivery is prospective. Do not convert editorial taxonomic gloss or Gray excerpts into Darwin-authored corpus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1575: May 29, 1854 inferred from Thursday May 25 Philosophical Club dinner; a separate missing nice little note supplies Hooker stomach illness. Darwin advises rest/exercise and recalls former heart trouble, then contrasts his own recent improvement with London visits. Season tickets bought for proposed Crystal Palace opening, not evidence the June opening already occurred. Forbes Edinburgh introductory lecture has been read from Horner newspaper loan; anniversary address merely heard praised. Next-year Chiswick trip, possible Kew lectureship and impending birth remain future. The current note is neither Hooker childbirth congratulations nor a response to later June letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1572: Saturday June 24 inferred from daughter born previous night, June 23. Hooker reports wife and baby doing well and his reading Brodie during childbirth, then explicitly asks Darwin meaning of highness/lowness in animals and explains plant organ specialisation and deviation from leaf type. Dinner reference concerns June 22, not May 25. Attached Darwin memorandum is a separate voice/layer outlining his answer, with uncertain note-writing time; do not fold it into Hooker prompt. Direct Darwin response is 1573.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1573: June 27, 1854 answers 1572 across childbirth, Brodie, dinner and explicit highness/lowness question. Chloroform is a question to Hooker, not a reported Hooker action yet. Darwin states ideas are eclectic and unclear, distinguishes within-kingdom differentiation, cross-kingdom comparison, retrograde development and physiological division of labour; preserve qualifications rather than replace with a settled ranking. Footnote quotations from other works and modern histories are not the response body. Hooker 1576 answers the chloroform question and elaborates the taxonomy debate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1576: Thursday June 29, 1854 follows June 27 answer. Hooker says he administered chloroform despite doctor prejudice and explicitly opposes Darwin gales-of-wind analogy. He argues Coniferae are genuine dicotyledons, temporarily allows a gymnosperm/angiosperm division, asks for botanical sources and disputes parallel series using mollusc/articulate comparisons. His strict all-members hierarchical view is not Darwin agreement. Wife improving and Saturday Kew return prospective; horticultural prospectus seeks wealthy subscribers. Separate Darwin notes include genealogical comparison and distinction between degradation and non-development; undated notes are not Hooker words or June 29 Darwin response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1577: July 7, 1854 directly answers 1576: delay due to visitors and illness, joking elastic-theory objection, requested botanical references recalled uncertainly, disagreement about comparing archetypes, larval/degradation distinction, ancient forms resembling embryos, rejection of parallelism and Forbes polarity. Keep uncertain memory and wrong Jussieu volume in original; correction belongs to apparatus. P8 offers conditional subscription or advertisement forwarding, not completed subscription/delivery. Contemporary sickness and caveats remain. Later Origin formulation in footnote is not current available source material.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1540: Previously accepted primary reading reused with exact note, ledger and raw source pins. November 5, 1853 gives explicit same-morning receipt and opening order: missing Sabine notice first, Hooker 1539 second. The same medal news produced a different emotional response through friendship. Lindley nomination, Mrs Hooker slow recovery, widened medal eligibility and foreign evidence specifically match 1539; gratitude is a direct answer. Sabine original is missing and must not be reconstructed. Finishing second volume is prospective; 1854 proofs are later apparatus. All body paragraphs read, with P4 valediction and P5–7 post-closing continuation retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1552F: Previously accepted primary reading reused with exact note, ledger and raw source pins. Thursday afternoon is one of two mutually exclusive dates, February 9 or 16, 1854, not a continuous date interval or an automatically chosen February 16. Book arrived within minutes. Darwin has seen dedication and some illustrations but has not read the title page or all illustrations; Emma then has the book. Reading this evening and setting aside Stansbury are intentions. Later March 7 and March 23 reading-notebook entries must not be imported as completed February reading. Mrs Hooker assistance is credited, not equal authorship of every page. No preserved covering incoming letter; reverse acknowledgement in 1557 answers his gratitude.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1557: Previously accepted primary reading reused with exact note, ledger and raw source pins. Sunday assigned February 26, 1854. P1 explicitly answers Darwin kind hearty acceptance of the dedication in 1552F and explains its Antarctic-voyage origin. P2 reflects on ambition and family, followed by wife health after a walk, response to Lyell lava-slope news, expected Henslow visit, Tasmania grant and six-copy obligation, and sold-out travels with profits still unknown. Only P1 is a demonstrated reply to 1552F. Lyell source letter identity remains ambiguous between January Madeira and a possible February Tenerife letter; no invented Darwin reading or exact cross-correspondent edge. Future delivery of Flora Tasmanica and unborn child are not accomplished facts. Undated Darwin marks separate.

reading_method: Nine targets independently read in full from preserved sources including all apparatus; three contexts reuse accepted current-period batch-01 primary reading with exact hashes. No figures in newly read targets. Worker report source/voice/date errors are explicitly corrected; its preserved drafts are not primary authority.
